category_title: Students with severe hearing impairment and EAL who use physical gestures and lip-reading to decipher archaic language
student_description: Andrius is a student with severe hearing impairment and EAL who is initially withdrawn and struggles significantly with traditional writing and verbal communication. He uniquely needs an environment that avoids forced group work and direct pronunciation corrections, thriving instead when given social autonomy and opportunities to express his understanding through drama, playfulness, and physical gestures.

criteria.rationale: Because his verbal communication is basic and he has EAL/HI, he needs explicit, repeated explanations of text to access the material.
criteria.check: The tutor provides detailed explanations, re-explanations, or clear breakdowns of specific words, lines, or concepts rather than assuming prior understanding.

criteria.rationale: Forced group work triggers a fear of judgment, so he requires the freedom to choose his own peers to feel comfortable.
criteria.check: The tutor offers the student a choice in who to work with or how to engage socially, rather than forcing a specific group assignment.

criteria.rationale: He thrives on independent perseverance and ignores direct pronunciation corrections, so the tutor must encourage rather than micromanage his speech.
criteria.check: The tutor provides general encouragement or steps back to let him work, and explicitly avoids correcting his pronunciation or enunciation.
